items.prompt:
An embryo is an organism in its:
A) Oldest stage
B) Earliest stage of development
C) Adult stage
D) Fossil stage

steps: An embryo is the earliest developmental stage.

items.prompt:
Scientists compare embryos of different species to find:
A) Their colors
B) Developmental similarities that show relationships
C) Their weights
D) Their names
items.answer: B) Developmental similarities that show relationships

items.prompt:
Many early vertebrate embryos share features such as a:
A) Beak
B) Tail
C) Shell
D) Flower

steps: Early vertebrate embryos often show a tail and similar segments.

items.prompt:
When very different adult animals have similar embryos, it suggests they:
A) Are unrelated
B) Share a common ancestor
C) Have no genes
D) Are nonliving

steps: Shared early development points to common ancestry.

items.prompt:
Why can embryos reveal relationships that adult anatomy hides?
A) Embryos are bigger
B) Embryos may show shared ancestral features that change by adulthood
C) Adults have no anatomy
D) Embryos never change
items.answer: B) Embryos may show shared ancestral features that change by adulthood

steps: Shared early features can disappear as the adult develops.

items.prompt:
What kind of data is used for embryological evidence?
A) Sound recordings
B) Displays (pictures) of embryos
C) Temperature logs
D) Rock samples

steps: Scientists analyze pictorial displays of embryos.

items.prompt:
Two embryos share many early structures but the adults look nothing alike. Best inference?
A) They are unrelated
B) They likely share a common ancestor despite different adult forms
C) Embryos are meaningless
D) They are the same age
items.answer: B) They likely share a common ancestor despite different adult forms

steps: Shared early development suggests relationship even when adults differ.

items.prompt:
Embryological evidence is valuable mainly because it:
A) Shows the weather
B) Can reveal relationships not evident in fully formed anatomy
C) Predicts the future
D) Replaces all other evidence
items.answer: B) Can reveal relationships not evident in fully formed anatomy

steps: Embryos expose shared features hidden in adults.
